title: Internal IT and workplace
description: Review the tools, devices and access employees use every day: device management, SaaS access, joiners, movers and leavers, and internal support.
expertises: SaaS access, identity and licence lifecycle
Internal IT support and workplace tools
questions: Which devices, accounts and SaaS tools does the change add, move or remove for employees?
How is access granted on arrival, changed on a move and removed on departure?
Who supports employees when the tool or device fails, and in what time?

sources.title: NIST SP 800-124 Rev. 2, Guidelines for Managing the Security of Mobile Devices in the Enterprise
NIST SP 800-46 Rev. 2, Guide to Enterprise Telework, Remote Access, and Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) Security
RFC 7644, System for Cross-domain Identity Management: Protocol

specialists.title: Endpoint and device manager
specialists.focus: Check that every device that reaches company data is enrolled, encrypted, patched and can be locked or wiped remotely, including personally owned devices.
checks: The device inventory matches the people who hold devices; unknown devices are listed.
Disk encryption, screen lock and automatic updates are enforced by policy, not by instruction.
Personally owned devices reach company data only through a managed app or profile that can be removed.

specialists.title: Identity and access administrator
specialists.focus: Map who gets which SaaS account and role, through which identity provider, and how access follows a joiner, a mover and a leaver.
checks: Each SaaS tool is connected to single sign-on, or the exception and its owner are recorded.
Provisioning and deprovisioning are automated where the tool supports it, for example through SCIM.
A leaver's accounts are disabled on the last day and the evidence is kept.

specialists.title: SaaS and licence manager
specialists.focus: Inventory the SaaS tools, their owners, licence counts and renewal dates, and find unused or duplicated subscriptions.
checks: Every tool has a business owner and a renewal date.
Assigned licences are compared with active users over the last 90 days.
A new tool is checked for data handling before employees can sign up with a company account.

specialists.title: Workplace support lead
specialists.focus: Define how employees ask for help, the response times, the self-service articles and what changes for the support team.
checks: Employees have one place to ask for help, and requests are tracked.
The change comes with a how-to article and a known-issues list for the internal helpdesk.
Loaner devices or a fallback exist for the people whose work stops when a device fails.

evidence: Device inventory and management console export for the population concerned.
List of SaaS tools with owners, licence counts, single sign-on status and renewal dates.
Joiner, mover and leaver procedure and a recent leaver's deprovisioning record.
Internal support request volumes and response times for the tools affected.
challenge: Which device or account would still reach company data after an employee leaves?
Does the change add a tool outside single sign-on that someone will forget to deprovision?
Can a lost laptop be wiped today, and who would do it on a weekend?
Is a new tool needed, or does an existing one already cover the need?
decision_criteria: Proceed when devices are managed, access follows the identity provider and the leaver process covers the new tool.
Revise when a tool or device reaches company data without enrolment, single sign-on or a named owner.
Ask for a pilot group when the change affects how everyone signs in or works on their device.
Name the measure, such as accounts open after departure or unmanaged devices, and its target.
